question: What reliable freshwater and riverine sources can accelerate Western Visayas (Panay) species coverage, and are site-level data publicly retrievable?

findings.sourceType: historical river-system biodiversity study; abstract/metadata evidence only
findings.siteAsReported: Jalaur River System, Iloilo, Panay Island; upper, middle and lower sampling areas are reported in the abstract.
findings.access: CPU institutional repository record provides abstract and citation. Direct repository page timed out during review; the publisher-hosted Silliman Journal PDF returned HTTP 502. Full paper, tables, exact methods, species list, station coordinates and rights were not inspected.
findings.interpretation: The aggregate demonstrates that a named Panay river study sampled fish spanning freshwater, brackish/marine-affinity and migratory categories. It is not a site-specific freshwater checklist. The abstract aggregate counts cannot be split into station-specific species records.

findings.sourceType: official research-output acquisition lead; no underlying dataset retrieved
findings.projectTitleAsReported: Morpho-functional traits and eDNA metabarcoding of freshwater fishes and invertebrate communities in Panay Island
findings.implementerAsReported: University of the Philippines Visayas (UPV), with DOST-PCAARRD support
plannedOutputsAsReported: protocol/reference manual for inland-water biological monitoring
voucher specimens deposited in natural-history museums
findings.access: Two official PCAARRD 2025 listings and a UP Visayas project-monitoring notice identify the project and expected outputs. These are metadata/status records, not the DNA library, taxa dataset, vouchers or final report.
findings.interpretation: This is the highest-priority current freshwater data-acquisition lead for V1 because the stated scope is Panay inland waters and the planned products include reference libraries and vouchers. Do not treat expected outputs as completed or available datasets until retrieved and checked.

officialRecords: The 2025 PCAARRD GIA list and its 2025 project/status table both report a project period of 2024-05-01 to 2026-04-30 and status ONGOING as of 2025-12-31.
statusAsReported.currentCompletion: The planned end date has passed as of this review (2026-10-30), but no final report, dataset or completion update was located in the records reviewed; actual completion and public availability remain unverified.

evidenceBoundary: No Jalaur fish names beyond Anguilla marmorata as stated in the abstract were transcribed; the 51-species total and habitat-affinity counts are aggregate source claims only.
No station coordinates, taxon-to-reach table, catch-event crosswalk, voucher accession list, or present-day observation was established.
The Jalaur study is historical and cannot establish current presence, abundance, diet, catchability, safety or legal access.
PCAARRD/UPV project output targets and status reports do not prove that the reference libraries, final report, or site-level taxa data are publicly available.
Rights for article-table reproduction and project data reuse were not verified; public-app publication is not approved.

disposition.reason: The Jalaur article was available only as abstract/metadata during this review, while the Panay freshwater project is an official output lead without an accessible final dataset or report.

nextAction: Prepare and send no message automatically: first obtain the final Panay freshwater biodiversity/DNA reference libraries, named waterbody/site list, species and barcode tables, marker and eDNA detection limitations, sample dates/coordinates, voucher/accession crosswalk, final report, reuse terms and current project status from UP Visayas and DOST-PCAARRD. In parallel, retrieve the full Jalaur article through an accessible institutional route and keep its freshwater, brackish and marine-affinity evidence separate.
